title: Chevron Is Offloading Hess Midstream and Taking a $3 Billion to $4 Billion Hit. Here's What It Means for CVX Stock.
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Chevron is divesting its ownership stake in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets in exchange for reduced tariff rates on midstream services in the Bakken through 2045. While the deal results in a $3-4 billion one-time after-tax loss, it will reduce Chevron's Bakken midstream costs by 50% and simplify its balance sheet by removing $3.7 billion in debt. Hess Midstream gains independence and diversification as a multi-basin operator, with the deal being accretive to both companies' shareholders long-term.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite the $3-4 billion one-time loss, Chevron benefits from 50% reduction in Bakken midstream costs, improved return on capital employed (0.5% accretive), simplified portfolio, $3.7 billion debt reduction, and locked-in long-term cost savings through 2045 that will enhance future free cash flow generation.

Hess Midstream achieves full independence, becomes a multi-basin operator with DJ Basin diversification, increases third-party revenue opportunities, and gains the ability to pursue additional acquisitions. The deal is per-share accretive after accounting for the 40% share count reduction, allowing the company to maintain its dividend.

title: Chevron's Portfolio Reshaping Strategy to Unlock Stronger Returns
author: Na

However, Chevron will record a one-time after-tax loss of $3-4 billion at closing. The transaction aims to improve capital efficiency and upstream returns.

title: HESM Q2 Beat Masks Lower Volumes as Second-Half Costs Move Higher
author: Na
description: Hess Midstream LP (HESM) beat Q2 2026 earnings expectations with 75 cents per share, up 1.4% YoY, despite lower throughput. Higher tariff rates and reduced operating costs offset weaker volumes. Management expects second-half improvement as Chevron wells come online, but Q3 Adjusted EBITDA is projected at $310-320 million as deferred maintenance and capital spending rise. Full-year guidance remains flat versus 2025.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed signals: Q2 beat supported by cost control and tariffs, but lower throughput and flat full-year guidance limit upside. Weak momentum and value scores, with execution risk in H2 as deferred maintenance and higher capex pressure cash flow.
Reported record Q2 Adjusted EBITDA of $2.8 billion, up 17% YoY, demonstrating stronger industry performance and providing favorable comparison context.
Raised 2026 free cash flow guidance to $1.1-1.3 billion after record Q2 Adjusted EBITDA, showing strong operational execution and improved capital allocation.

title: Got $10,000 to Invest in This High-Yield, Midstream Stock? Here's What It Could Be Worth in 10 Years.
author: Selena Maranjian
description: Hess Midstream LP (HESM) is highlighted as an attractive midstream energy investment opportunity, offering a 7.7% dividend yield with quarterly increases over nine years. The company operates oil, gas, and produced water handling assets in North Dakota's Bakken and Three Forks Shale plays. Its corporate structure was restructured in 2019 to simplify tax treatment for investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents HESM favorably, highlighting its attractive 7.7% dividend yield, consistent quarterly dividend increases over nine years, and strategic assets in a prolific oil basin. The simplified tax structure is also presented as an advantage for investors.
Chevron is mentioned only as the acquirer of Hess in 2025, with no sentiment expressed regarding the acquisition or Chevron's operations.

title: This Overlooked Pipeline Stock Quietly Raised Its Dividend Again. Almost Nobody Covered It. (It's Now Yielding Nearly 8%!)
author: Selena Maranjian
description: Hess Midstream LP (HESM), a pipeline company processing natural gas from North Dakota's Bakken and Three Forks Shale regions, has quietly maintained a strong dividend yield of 7.8% with consistent quarterly increases over nine years. The company has also engaged in share buybacks and has benefited from geopolitical tensions, with energy sector tailwinds boosting related stocks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company demonstrates strong dividend fundamentals with a 7.8% yield, nine years of consistent quarterly dividend increases (7% year-over-year and 56% over five years), active share buyback program, and recent 21% year-to-date stock appreciation benefiting from energy sector tailwinds.

Chevron is mentioned as benefiting from geopolitical tensions (Iran conflict) with a 36% year-to-date gain as of August 31, 2026, and is noted as the parent company of Hess (which operates through Hess Midstream).
